sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Copying arrays might seem simple, but there are important details to master. Let's break it down!

• How to properly duplicate array contents
• The difference between shallow and deep copies
• Common mistakes to avoid when copying arrays

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you have a tray of cookies (your array). If you want to share them with a friend, you might:

• Point to the same tray (this is like copying the reference)
• Make a new tray with identical cookies (this is a proper copy)

In Java, arrays are objects, so simply assigning one array to another doesn't create a new copy - it just creates another reference to the same array!

• **Shallow Copy**: Creates a new array but shares the same elements
• **Deep Copy**: Creates a completely independent copy with new elements
• **Common Methods**: Using loops, `clone()`, or `System.arraycopy()`

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Assigning one array variable to another copies the reference, not the array contents
To copy array contents, use a loop or System.arraycopy(src, srcPos, dest, destPos, length)
Arrays.copyOf(original, newLength) creates a new array with a copy of the elements
After a reference copy, both variables point to the same array object
Modifying elements through one reference is visible through the other

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Copying arrays requires creating new array objects, not just new references. Use System.arraycopy() or clone() for primitive arrays. Practice creating independent copies to avoid bugs. Ready to learn about passing arrays to methods next.

questions.question: What happens when you assign one array variable to another (e.g., arr2 = arr1)?
options: Both variables reference the same array object
A new array is created automatically
questions.explanation: Assigning arr2 = arr1 copies the reference, not the array contents. Both variables now point to the same array object in memory.

questions.question: Which method can be used to properly copy array contents?
questions.explanation: System.arraycopy() properly copies array contents from one array to another. A simple assignment only copies the reference, not the actual elements.
